correctness.rationale: For every t>=2, all size-t matchings on 2t vertices are perfect. Incidence/parity gives precisely A,B for the cycle and one-chord graph, and precisely A,B,T union {x,y} for the two-chord graph. The one-chord complex is a cone on an unused edge. Factoring the disjoint odd matching B reduces the final complex to L on T,U,W. For t=2 L is S0*S0=S1. For t>=3, L is the union of two explicit contractible subcomplexes whose exact intersection is the sphere S^{t-2}; the CW homotopy pushout gives L~S^{t-1}. Joining with boundary of the t-vertex B simplex gives S^{2t-2}. General proof is integral and includes t=2 boundary. Independent incidence, Euler and mod-two homology checks for 2<=t<=7 agree; finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The original cycle homotopy sphere is explicitly credited to prior work. The first public motivating 2026 theorem applies to edge insertions that preserve bipartiteness; neither of the two chords in the claim preserves bipartiteness. The exhaustive published-source comparison of the relevant theorem, its predecessor on full graphs, and the general Leray bounds found no identical all-t intermediate contractibility plus dimension-increasing recovery statement. The sparse two-chorded family for all t>=3 is not an instance of existing K_n/K_{r,s} complete-graph formulas; vanishing bounds cannot supply homotopy equivalences.

value.rationale: This infinite natural family diagnoses the precise bipartiteness boundary in the current homology-persistence theorem: a length-two same-parity chord kills the top integral sphere class completely; the complementary same-parity chord then creates a new topological sphere one dimension higher. The full three-stage integral homotopy calculation—not merely a single negative test—shows a nonmonotone and dimension-shifting response to consecutive graph edge insertions. It supplies an explicit model and proof technique for investigating nonbipartite edge-addition transitions. The t=2 special case is old, but t>=3 gives unbounded distinct graph orders.
